name: Conflict-Check Engine

parameters.content:
## Conflict-Check Engine

### How it works

This workflow has TWO independent parts on one canvas:

**A. Run a conflict check (top row)**
Fires when staff submit a new client/party name (plus any known adverse parties) for a conflict check, usually before formally opening a matter. Fuzzy-matches every submitted name against every existing Clio contact and every matter's client name and description, logs the check and its results to an audit sheet, and emails the requesting attorney a report — with click-through links to record whether they're clearing it or escalating it for a closer look.

**B. Record the attorney's decision (bottom row)**
A webhook fired by clicking one of the report email's two links. Updates the audit log with the decision and shows a confirmation page.

**This never clears or blocks anything on its own.** It only ever surfaces potential matches with a similarity score — the attorney reviews every result and makes the actual conflict determination. There is no code path here that auto-approves a new matter or auto-declines one; that judgment call belongs to the attorney every time (ABA Op. 512 — this surfaces information, it never makes a legal or ethical determination).

**Fuzzy matching here is name-similarity only, not a legal conflicts analysis.** It catches spelling variations, maiden names, abbreviated company suffixes, and a submitted name appearing inside a matter's description — it cannot catch a conflict that requires actual legal judgment (e.g. a corporate subsidiary relationship, or a beneficial-ownership conflict) unless a name literally matches. Treat 'no matches found' as 'nothing matched by name,' not 'no conflict exists.'

### Setup steps

- [ ] Set up the Bar-Compliance Guardrail (NTC-33) first — the report email's audit logging goes through it.
- [ ] Create a Google Sheet with a 'Conflict Checks' tab — see the deploy guide for exact columns.
- [ ] Configure Clio OAuth2, Google Sheets OAuth2, and SMTP credentials.
- [ ] Wire your intake process (a Fluent Forms form, or any tool staff use before opening a matter) to POST to this workflow's webhook URL.
- [ ] Set the required n8n Variables: CLIO_BASE_URL, FIRM_NAME, FIRM_EMAIL, FIRM_FROM_EMAIL, GUARDRAIL_WORKFLOW_ID, CONFLICT_LOG_SHEET_ID, CONFLICT_DECISION_WEBHOOK_URL (copy this after activating).
- [ ] Optionally tune CONFLICT_MATCH_THRESHOLD (default 0.6 — lower catches more, with more false positives).
- [ ] Activate the workflow.

### Customization

CONFLICT_MATCH_THRESHOLD is the entire sensitivity dial — this is a 'surface everything plausible' tool, so most firms should err toward a lower threshold (more false positives) rather than risk missing a real conflict. Firms with over 200 contacts or matters will need pagination added to the two Clio fetch nodes (not built here).

## Fuzzy-match a new name against the whole firm

Checks every submitted name against every Clio contact and matter, scores by similarity, and logs the check for audit before emailing the report.

## Record the attorney's decision — a second, independent branch

A webhook fired by clicking Clear or Escalate in the report email. Only ever updates the audit log — never blocks or approves anything itself.

nodes.name: When Conflict Check Requested
nodes.notes: Wire this to whatever staff use before opening a matter — a Fluent Forms conflict-check form is the simplest option. Expects: new_client_name, adverse_party_names (comma-separated), matter_description, requested_by_email.

nodes.name: Parse Conflict Check Request
nodes.notes: At least one name is required — the new client's name alone is enough to run a check, adverse parties are optional extras.

nodes.name: Is Valid Conflict Check Request
nodes.notes: True continues to run the actual match; false means the submission had no names at all and just gets acknowledged.

nodes.name: Respond Invalid Request
nodes.notes: Acknowledges an empty/malformed submission rather than silently doing nothing.

nodes.name: Fetch All Firm Contacts From Clio
nodes.notes: Every contact in Clio — clients, related parties, everyone — is fair game for a conflict match. Firms with over 200 contacts need pagination added (not built here).

nodes.name: Fetch All Firm Matters From Clio
nodes.notes: Deliberately not filtered by status -- a closed matter's adverse party is still a real conflict risk years later. Solo/small firms won't hit the 200-matter cap; larger ones will need pagination added.

nodes.name: Run Fuzzy Conflict Match
nodes.notes: The whole matching engine lives here. CONFLICT_MATCH_THRESHOLD (0-1) controls sensitivity — lower catches more names at the cost of more false positives; this tool is meant to over-surface, not under-surface.

nodes.name: Assign Conflict Check ID
nodes.notes: This ID is what ties the audit log row to whichever decision link the attorney eventually clicks.

nodes.name: Log Conflict Check For Audit
nodes.notes: Every conflict check gets a permanent audit row here, regardless of whether anything matched — being able to prove a check was run is as important as the result itself. Column headers must match exactly.

nodes.name: Build Conflict Report Email
nodes.notes: CONFLICT_DECISION_WEBHOOK_URL must be set to this workflow's own Production URL for 'When Conflict Decision Is Made' — copy it after activating. Reads deal fields back from 'Assign Conflict Check ID' by name, not $json, since the Sheets append node in between echoes back a flattened row, not the original structured data.

nodes.name: Log Conflict Report For Compliance Audit
nodes.notes: Fire-and-forget audit logging only — this goes to firm staff, not a client, so the guardrail's approval result is deliberately ignored, same internal-notification pattern used throughout this catalog.

nodes.name: Send Conflict Report Email
nodes.notes: Reaches back to 'Build Conflict Report Email' by name, not $json, since the guardrail call in between replaces $json with its own response.

nodes.name: Respond Conflict Check Submitted
nodes.notes: Acknowledges the original submission — staff get the check_id back immediately, the full report follows by email.

nodes.name: When Conflict Decision Is Made
nodes.notes: This is the URL the two links in the report email point to — copy its Production URL into CONFLICT_DECISION_WEBHOOK_URL after activating.

nodes.name: Parse Conflict Decision Request
nodes.notes: Pulls check_id and action (clear/escalate) out of the query string and validates both are present.

nodes.name: If Decision Request Valid
nodes.notes: True continues to look up the check; false means the link is malformed or missing a required parameter.

nodes.name: Respond Invalid Decision Link
nodes.notes: Plain error page for a malformed or incomplete decision link.

nodes.name: Read Conflict Check Log
nodes.notes: Reads every logged conflict check so the specific one referenced by check_id can be found.

nodes.name: Find Matching Conflict Check Row
nodes.notes: Matches the decision link's check_id against the audit log by exact string equality.

nodes.name: If Conflict Check Found
nodes.notes: True continues to record the decision; false means the check_id doesn't match any logged row (already resolved, or a malformed link).

parameters.responseBody: We couldn't find that conflict check — it may have already been resolved or the link is malformed.

nodes.name: Respond Check Not Found
nodes.notes: Plain error page — nothing in the log gets changed when this fires.

nodes.name: Update Conflict Check With Decision
nodes.notes: Only ever records the attorney's decision — there is no code path anywhere in this workflow that opens, blocks, or auto-approves a matter based on this.

parameters.responseBody:
={{ '

' + ($json.action === 'clear' ? '✅ Marked cleared' : '🔺 Marked for escalation') + '

Recorded for ' + $json.names_checked + '.

' }}

nodes.name: Respond Decision Confirmation Page
nodes.notes: Plain confirmation page — no further automated action happens after this.

description: Runs on two independent webhooks. Conflict check: fuzzy-matches every submitted name (new client plus known adverse parties) against every Clio contact and every matter's client name and description, logs the check and its results to an audit sheet, and emails the requesting attorney a report with Clear/Escalate decision links. Decision: records whichever link was clicked in the audit log. Never clears or blocks a matter automatically -- the attorney always makes the actual conflict determination (ABA Op. 512). Replaces manual conflict checks and PM add-ons, catching matches a manual review misses.
